extracted.intended_audience: PSC staff, regulated utilities, and members of the public interested in New York State rulemaking and notice-and-comment under SAPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on State Administrative Procedure Act (SAPA) requirements as applied to the New York Public Service Commission (PSC), including which PSC actions require SAPA, publication and filing obligations, and public comment timeframes. Useful for agency staff, regulated entities, and potential commenters preparing or responding to rulemaking notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSC obligation to follow SAPA and submit notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSC is obligated to follow prescribed SAPA procedures in the exercise of its decision making. The basic provisions applicable to the adoption of a rule requires the PSC to submit a notice of proposed rulemaking for publication in the State Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most actions taken by the PSC are subject to SAPA requirements. The Department of State produces the weekly New York State Register, which contains notices of newly proposed rules and proposed changes to existing rules; publication in the Register is the formal channel for proposing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public comment period — 60 days (with hearing extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency must offer the public an opportunity to comment on the proposal for a minimum period of 60 days after the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is required, the comment period extends to 5 days after the last public hearing before the agency may take action to adopt the proposal. Ensure comment windows are calculated from the Register publication date and account for any hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Revised Rule Making when final rule is substantially different (30-day comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the final rule will be substantially different from the proposed rule, the agency must publish a 'Notice of Revised Rule Making' and accept public comment for at least another 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial changes to a proposed rule trigger an additional formal notice and a fresh minimum comment period (>=30 days) so the public can review and comment on the revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing full text and publishing Notice of Adoption upon adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: If adopted, the agency must file the full text of the rule with the Department of State. At the same time, a 'Notice of Adoption' is published in the Register, indicating that the proposal has in fact been adopted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the full text with the Department of State and publishing the Notice of Adoption are required steps to finalize rulemaking under SAPA and to provide the public with the adopted rule text and formal notice of adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on re-adoption after withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proposal is withdrawn, the agency cannot adopt the same or a similar proposal without first providing the public with another opportunity to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal does not permit immediate re-adoption; agencies must re-open notice-and-comment if they intend to pursue a substantially similar proposal after withdrawal, ensuring meaningful public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Commission actions requiring SAPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists department matters requiring SAPA compliance, including: Amendments to the Commission rules (16 NYCRR); Tariff filings for Electric, Gas, Steam and Water (telephone tariffs are exempt); Interconnection Agreements; Waivers of Commission Rules; Financings; Most Commission-initiated proceedings; Orders directing utilities to take substantive actions; Rate cases; Modifications of Commission orders, if such orders adopted rules; Petitions for rehearing (if the Commission's order adopted a rule and if the Commission might grant the petition in whole or in part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to determine whether a PSC action triggers SAPA procedural obligations. Note the explicit exemption for telephone tariffs and the conditional application for petitions for rehearing and modifications that relate to adopted rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find PSC SAPA notices (State Register)
rubrics_metrics.description: PSC SAPA notices are available on the NY State Department of State website: NYS Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the weekly New York State Register (produced by the Department of State) to find notices of proposed rules, Notices of Revised Rule Making, and Notices of Adoption relevant to the PSC.
